  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

"""Model routing for all LLM calls.

    call_cheap(prompt, json_schema=None, feature=...)   bulk extraction / classification
    call_strong(prompt, json_schema=None, feature=...)  complex reasoning

Every call is logged to SQLite table `llm_usage` with token counts and an
estimated USD cost, tagged by `feature`, so cost can be reported per feature.

Configuration (backend/.env):
    GEMINI_API_KEY        required
    GEMINI_CHEAP_MODEL    default gemini-2.5-flash
    GEMINI_STRONG_MODEL   default gemini-2.5-pro
    GEMINI_CHEAP_THINKING thinking level for call_cheap on Gemini 3+ models (default low)
    GEMINI_BACKEND        auto (default) | vertex | gemini
                          auto = Vertex AI if the key starts with "AQ.", else Gemini API
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import os
import random
import sqlite3
import time
from contextlib import closing
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from google import genai
from google.genai import errors, types

from backend.data.prices import DB_PATH

BACKEND_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
load_dotenv(BACKEND_DIR / ".env")

CHEAP_MODEL = os.getenv("GEMINI_CHEAP_MODEL", "gemini-2.5-flash")
STRONG_MODEL = os.getenv("GEMINI_STRONG_MODEL", "gemini-2.5-pro")
CHEAP_THINKING = os.getenv("GEMINI_CHEAP_THINKING", "low")

MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5
BASE_BACKOFF = 2.0                       # seconds, doubled each retry, plus jitter
RETRYABLE_CODES = {429, 500, 502, 503, 504}
REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000             # per request; overloaded models otherwise hang for minutes

# USD per 1M tokens (input, output). Thinking tokens are billed as output.
# Standard paid-tier list prices for prompts <= 200k tokens; update if pricing changes.
PRICING = {
    "gemini-2.5-flash": (0.30, 2.50),
    "gemini-2.5-flash-lite": (0.10, 0.40),
    "gemini-2.5-pro": (1.25, 10.00),
}
DEFAULT_PRICE = PRICING["gemini-2.5-flash"]   # used (with a warning) for unlisted models

log = logging.getLogger("finn.llm")
_unpriced_warned: set[str] = set()


class LLMError(RuntimeError):
    pass


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Client
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def get_client() -> genai.Client:
    api_key = os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY")
    if not api_key:
        raise LLMError("GEMINI_API_KEY is not set (expected in backend/.env)")
    backend = os.getenv("GEMINI_BACKEND", "auto").lower()
    use_vertex = backend == "vertex" or (backend == "auto" and api_key.startswith("AQ."))
    # Disable the SDK's own silent retries so our logged backoff is the only retry layer.
    http_options = types.HttpOptions(timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS, retry_options=types.HttpRetryOptions(attempts=1))
    if use_vertex:
        return genai.Client(vertexai=True, api_key=api_key, http_options=http_options)
    return genai.Client(api_key=api_key, http_options=http_options)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Usage logging
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _connect() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    DB_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    conn.execute(
        """
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS llm_usage (
            id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            feature       TEXT NOT NULL,
            model         TEXT NOT NULL,
            input_tokens  INTEGER NOT NULL,
            output_tokens INTEGER NOT NULL,   -- includes thinking tokens
            est_cost_usd  REAL NOT NULL,
            created_at    TEXT NOT NULL       -- UTC ISO timestamp
        )
        """
    )
    return conn


def estimate_cost(model: str, input_tokens: int, output_tokens: int) -> float:
    price_in, price_out = PRICING.get(model, DEFAULT_PRICE)
    return (input_tokens * price_in + output_tokens * price_out) / 1_000_000


def log_usage(feature: str, model: str, input_tokens: int, output_tokens: int) -> float:
    if model not in PRICING and model not in _unpriced_warned:
        _unpriced_warned.add(model)
        log.warning("No price listed for %s; estimating with gemini-2.5-flash rates.", model)
    cost = estimate_cost(model, input_tokens, output_tokens)
    with closing(_connect()) as conn:
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO llm_usage (feature, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, est_cost_usd, created_at) "
            "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (feature, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost,
             datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")),
        )
        conn.commit()
    return cost


def usage_summary() -> list[dict]:
    """Totals per feature and model (for reporting)."""
    with closing(_connect()) as conn:
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        rows = conn.execute(
            """
            SELECT feature, model, COUNT(*) AS calls, SUM(input_tokens) AS input_tokens,
                   SUM(output_tokens) AS output_tokens, SUM(est_cost_usd) AS est_cost_usd
            FROM llm_usage GROUP BY feature, model ORDER BY feature, model
            """
        ).fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Calls
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _thinking_config(model: str, level: str | None) -> types.ThinkingConfig | None:
    """Keep thinking (billed as output tokens) small for bulk calls."""
    if level is None:
        return None
    if model.startswith("gemini-2.5-flash"):
        return types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_budget=0)       # 2.5 Flash: thinking off
    if model.startswith("gemini-2."):
        return None                                           # 2.5 Pro can't disable thinking
    return types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level=level)         # Gemini 3+


def _call(model: str, prompt: str, json_schema: dict | None, feature: str, temperature: float,
          thinking: str | None = None):
    config = types.GenerateContentConfig(temperature=temperature, thinking_config=_thinking_config(model, thinking))
    if json_schema is not None:
        config.response_mime_type = "application/json"
        config.response_json_schema = json_schema

    delay = BASE_BACKOFF
    for attempt in range(1, MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1):
        try:
            response = get_client().models.generate_content(model=model, contents=prompt, config=config)
            break
        except errors.APIError as exc:
            if exc.code not in RETRYABLE_CODES or attempt == MAX_ATTEMPTS:
                raise LLMError(f"{model} failed ({exc.code}): {exc.message}") from exc
            wait = delay + random.uniform(0, 1)
            log.warning("%s returned %s; retrying in %.1fs (attempt %d/%d)", model, exc.code, wait, attempt, MAX_ATTEMPTS)
            time.sleep(wait)
            delay *= 2

    usage = response.usage_metadata
    input_tokens = (usage.prompt_token_count or 0) if usage else 0
    output_tokens = ((usage.candidates_token_count or 0) + (usage.thoughts_token_count or 0)) if usage else 0
    log_usage(feature, model, input_tokens, output_tokens)

    text = response.text or ""
    if json_schema is None:
        return text
    try:
        return json.loads(text)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        raise LLMError(f"{model} returned invalid JSON: {text[:200]}") from exc


def call_cheap(prompt: str, json_schema: dict | None = None, feature: str = "unspecified",
               temperature: float = 0.0):
    """Fast, low-cost model. Returns parsed JSON if `json_schema` is given, else text."""
    return _call(CHEAP_MODEL, prompt, json_schema, feature, temperature, thinking=CHEAP_THINKING)


def call_strong(prompt: str, json_schema: dict | None = None, feature: str = "unspecified",
                temperature: float = 0.2):
    """Most capable model, for complex reasoning. Same return contract as call_cheap."""
    return _call(STRONG_MODEL, prompt, json_schema, feature, temperature)

"""Model routing for all LLM calls.

    call_cheap(prompt, json_schema=None, feature=...)   bulk extraction / classification
    call_strong(prompt, json_schema=None, feature=...)  complex reasoning

Every call is logged to SQLite table `llm_usage` with token counts and an
estimated USD cost, tagged by `feature`, so cost can be reported per feature.

Configuration (backend/.env):
    GEMINI_API_KEY        required
    GEMINI_CHEAP_MODEL    default gemini-2.5-flash
    GEMINI_STRONG_MODEL   default gemini-2.5-pro
    GEMINI_CHEAP_THINKING thinking level for call_cheap on Gemini 3+ models (default low)
    GEMINI_BACKEND        auto (default) | vertex | gemini
                          auto = Vertex AI if the key starts with "AQ.", else Gemini API
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import os
import random
import sqlite3
import time
from contextlib import closing
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from google import genai
from google.genai import errors, types

from backend.data.prices import DB_PATH

BACKEND_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
load_dotenv(BACKEND_DIR / ".env")

CHEAP_MODEL = os.getenv("GEMINI_CHEAP_MODEL", "gemini-2.5-flash")
STRONG_MODEL = os.getenv("GEMINI_STRONG_MODEL", "gemini-2.5-pro")
CHEAP_THINKING = os.getenv("GEMINI_CHEAP_THINKING", "low")

MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5
BASE_BACKOFF = 2.0                       # seconds, doubled each retry, plus jitter
RETRYABLE_CODES = {429, 500, 502, 503, 504}
REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000             # per request; overloaded models otherwise hang for minutes

# USD per 1M tokens (input, output). Thinking tokens are billed as output.
# Standard paid-tier list prices for prompts <= 200k tokens; update if pricing changes.
PRICING = {
    "gemini-2.5-flash": (0.30, 2.50),
    "gemini-2.5-flash-lite": (0.10, 0.40),
    "gemini-2.5-pro": (1.25, 10.00),
}
DEFAULT_PRICE = PRICING["gemini-2.5-flash"]   # used (with a warning) for unlisted models

log = logging.getLogger("finn.llm")
_unpriced_warned: set[str] = set()


class LLMError(RuntimeError):
    pass


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Client
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def get_client() -> genai.Client:
    api_key = os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY")
    if not api_key:
        raise LLMError("GEMINI_API_KEY is not set (expected in backend/.env)")
    backend = os.getenv("GEMINI_BACKEND", "auto").lower()
    use_vertex = backend == "vertex" or (backend == "auto" and api_key.startswith("AQ."))
    # Disable the SDK's own silent retries so our logged backoff is the only retry layer.
    http_options = types.HttpOptions(timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS, retry_options=types.HttpRetryOptions(attempts=1))
    if use_vertex:
        return genai.Client(vertexai=True, api_key=api_key, http_options=http_options)
    return genai.Client(api_key=api_key, http_options=http_options)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Usage logging
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _connect() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    DB_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    conn.execute(
        """
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS llm_usage (
            id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            feature       TEXT NOT NULL,
            model         TEXT NOT NULL,
            input_tokens  INTEGER NOT NULL,
            output_tokens INTEGER NOT NULL,   -- includes thinking tokens
            est_cost_usd  REAL NOT NULL,
            created_at    TEXT NOT NULL       -- UTC ISO timestamp
        )
        """
    )
    return conn


def estimate_cost(model: str, input_tokens: int, output_tokens: int) -> float:
    price_in, price_out = PRICING.get(model, DEFAULT_PRICE)
    return (input_tokens * price_in + output_tokens * price_out) / 1_000_000


def log_usage(feature: str, model: str, input_tokens: int, output_tokens: int) -> float:
    if model not in PRICING and model not in _unpriced_warned:
        _unpriced_warned.add(model)
        log.warning("No price listed for %s; estimating with gemini-2.5-flash rates.", model)
    cost = estimate_cost(model, input_tokens, output_tokens)
    with closing(_connect()) as conn:
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO llm_usage (feature, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, est_cost_usd, created_at) "
            "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (feature, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost,
             datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")),
        )
        conn.commit()
    return cost


def usage_summary() -> list[dict]:
    """Totals per feature and model (for reporting)."""
    with closing(_connect()) as conn:
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        rows = conn.execute(
            """
            SELECT feature, model, COUNT(*) AS calls, SUM(input_tokens) AS input_tokens,
                   SUM(output_tokens) AS output_tokens, SUM(est_cost_usd) AS est_cost_usd
            FROM llm_usage GROUP BY feature, model ORDER BY feature, model
            """
        ).fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Calls
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _thinking_config(model: str, level: str | None) -> types.ThinkingConfig | None:
    """Keep thinking (billed as output tokens) small for bulk calls."""
    if level is None:
        return None
    if model.startswith("gemini-2.5-flash"):
        return types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_budget=0)       # 2.5 Flash: thinking off
    if model.startswith("gemini-2."):
        return None                                           # 2.5 Pro can't disable thinking
    return types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level=level)         # Gemini 3+


def _call(model: str, prompt: str, json_schema: dict | None, feature: str, temperature: float,
          thinking: str | None = None):
    config = types.GenerateContentConfig(temperature=temperature, thinking_config=_thinking_config(model, thinking))
    if json_schema is not None:
        config.response_mime_type = "application/json"
        config.response_json_schema = json_schema

    delay = BASE_BACKOFF
    for attempt in range(1, MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1):
        try:
            response = get_client().models.generate_content(model=model, contents=prompt, config=config)
            break
        except (errors.APIError, httpx.TimeoutException, httpx.TransportError) as exc:
            code = getattr(exc, "code", None) or type(exc).__name__   # network errors have no HTTP code
            retryable = not isinstance(exc, errors.APIError) or exc.code in RETRYABLE_CODES
            if not retryable or attempt == MAX_ATTEMPTS:
                raise LLMError(f"{model} failed ({code}): {getattr(exc, 'message', None) or exc}") from exc
            wait = delay + random.uniform(0, 1)
            log.warning("%s returned %s; retrying in %.1fs (attempt %d/%d)", model, code, wait, attempt, MAX_ATTEMPTS)
            time.sleep(wait)
            delay *= 2

    usage = response.usage_metadata
    input_tokens = (usage.prompt_token_count or 0) if usage else 0
    output_tokens = ((usage.candidates_token_count or 0) + (usage.thoughts_token_count or 0)) if usage else 0
    log_usage(feature, model, input_tokens, output_tokens)

    text = response.text or ""
    if json_schema is None:
        return text
    try:
        return json.loads(text)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        raise LLMError(f"{model} returned invalid JSON: {text[:200]}") from exc


def call_cheap(prompt: str, json_schema: dict | None = None, feature: str = "unspecified",
               temperature: float = 0.0):
    """Fast, low-cost model. Returns parsed JSON if `json_schema` is given, else text."""
    return _call(CHEAP_MODEL, prompt, json_schema, feature, temperature, thinking=CHEAP_THINKING)


def call_strong(prompt: str, json_schema: dict | None = None, feature: str = "unspecified",
                temperature: float = 0.2):
    """Most capable model, for complex reasoning. Same return contract as call_cheap."""
    return _call(STRONG_MODEL, prompt, json_schema, feature, temperature)

import sqlite3
c = sqlite3.connect("backend/data/finn.db"); c.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
Q = """SELECT a.ticker, substr(a.announced_at,1,10) d, a.subject, substr(a.description,1,90) descr, i.category, i.method,
       i.priority_score s, i.market_boost b, i.reaction_change_pct ch, i.reaction_volume_ratio vr, i.tier, i.summary
       FROM announcements a JOIN announcement_insights i ON i.announcement_id=a.id"""
seen = set()
def show(where, n):
    for r in c.execute(Q + " WHERE " + where + " ORDER BY i.priority_score DESC, a.announced_at DESC"):
        key = (r["ticker"], r["category"])
        if key in seen: continue
        seen.add(key); n -= 1
        ch = f"{r['ch']:+.1f}%/{r['vr']:.1f}x" if r["ch"] is not None and r["vr"] is not None else "-"
        print(f"{r['tier']:<13}{r['s']:>3} (+{r['b']}) {r['ticker']:<11}{r['category']:<18}{r['method']:<6}{ch:<13}| {r['subject'][:45]} | {r['descr']}")
        if r["summary"]: print(f"{'':<17}-> {r['summary']}")
        if n == 0: return
show("i.tier='MUST_READ'", 4)
show("i.tier='WORTH_A_LOOK'", 4)

cd "C:/Users/tanis/Downloads/FINN" && cat >> DECISIONS.md <<'EOF'

## D18 — LLM routing (`backend/llm.py`) and the model switch

- **Decision:** one module owns every LLM call. `call_cheap()` handles bulk
  classification/summaries; `call_strong()` handles complex reasoning. Both take an
  optional JSON schema (strict JSON output), retry 429/5xx and network
  timeouts with exponential backoff and jitter (5 attempts), and log every call
  to `llm_usage(feature, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, est_cost_usd,
  created_at)`. Thinking tokens are counted as output, which is how they're billed.
- **Config lives in `backend/.env`:** `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_BACKEND`
  (auto|vertex|gemini), `GEMINI_CHEAP_MODEL`, `GEMINI_STRONG_MODEL`,
  `GEMINI_CHEAP_THINKING`. Defaults follow the spec (`auto`: an `AQ.` key goes to
  Vertex; `gemini-2.5-flash` / `gemini-2.5-pro`).
- **What actually happened (14 Nov 2026):**
  - Vertex AI with the `AQ.` key returned 403: the Vertex/"Agent Platform" API
    isn't enabled on the key's Google Cloud project.
  - The same key works on the regular Gemini API, but there `gemini-2.5-flash`
    and `gemini-2.5-pro` return 404 "no longer available to new users".
  - We therefore run `GEMINI_BACKEND=gemini`. The cheap model was first
    `gemini-3.8-flash` (user's choice), but it was overloaded: repeated 503
    errors, a 504 after 58s, and roughly 5 minutes per batch. It was switched to
    `gemini-3.5-flash`, which answered in 9–28s. Both are just `.env` values.
  - The strong model is still undecided (`gemini-4-argon` returned 429 quota);
    it isn't needed until a later step.
- **SDK retries disabled:** the google-genai SDK's own silent retries are turned
  off, and each request has a 120s timeout, so our logged backoff is the only
  retry layer and an overloaded model can't hang the pipeline for minutes.
- **Cost estimates are approximate for Gemini 3.x:** `PRICING` lists only the
  2.5 models' list prices. Unlisted models are estimated at 2.5-flash rates
  ($0.30 / $2.50 per 1M tokens), with a warning. Token counts are exact; update
  `PRICING` before reporting dollar figures in Step 12.

## D19 — Classification: rules first, cheap LLM only for leftovers

- **Step A, rules (free):** ordered regex rules run over `subject + description`.
  When the subject is a generic label ("Updates", "General Updates", "Outcome
  of Board Meeting"), only the description is used. Order matters:
  transcripts/recordings → `earnings_call` before results; newspaper ads of
  results → `routine` before `results`. A board-meeting *intimation* is
  `routine` unless it announces a fund raise, bonus/split, M&A or dividend.
  ESG ratings are excluded from `credit_rating`.
- **Step B, cheap LLM:** rows with no rule match go to `call_cheap`, 20 per call,
  with an enum-constrained JSON schema. The model returns batch indices, not
  free-text IDs, so it can't invent IDs.
- **Result:** 224 / 281 (80%) handled by rules, 57 by the LLM (4 classify calls).
  The LLM rows were genuinely ambiguous: "General Updates", committee-meeting
  outcomes, rumour/news verifications, "Allotment of Securities pursuant to
  Non Convertible Securities" (NSE's label is used for both NCDs and ESOPs).
  9 rows remain `unclassified` even for the LLM; they are vague
  "Disclosure under Regulation 30" filings.
- **Caching:** results are stored in `announcement_insights` keyed by
  announcement id. Classification and summaries are never redone (`--force`
  resets). A run that is interrupted resumes where it stopped (rows wait as
  `pending_llm`).

## D20 — Priority score and tiers

- **Score = category weight + materiality bump + market boost, capped 0–100.**
  - Category weights: results 75; M&A 65; fund_raise, management_change,
    litigation, bonus_split 60; capex 50; credit_rating, dividend 45;
    insider_trading, earnings_call 40; press_release, unclassified 30;
    investor_meetings 15; routine 5.
  - Materiality bumps: CEO/MD/CFO/chairman change +10; dilutive equity raise
    (QIP, preferential, rights) +15; actual merger/demerger/scheme/open offer
    +10; rating upgrade/downgrade +15; SEBI/court/fraud litigation +10. This
    separates an NBFC's routine NCD allotment (60) from a QIP (75), and a new
    subsidiary (65) from a merger (75).
  - Market boost (max +25): taken from the *reaction session* (the first
    trading session after the announcement; after 15:30 IST it's the next
    day). +10/+15 for a |move| ≥ 3% / 5%, and +10/+15 for volume ≥ 1.5x / 2.5x
    the 20-day average (same definitions as `prices.get_metrics`).
- **Tiers:** ≥70 MUST_READ, 40–69 WORTH_A_LOOK, <40 ROUTINE.
- **Why reaction-session rather than "latest" price data:** a filing from three
  weeks ago should be judged by how the market reacted to it, not by today's tape.
- **Attribution fix:** the first version boosted 139/281 rows. Every filing
  on a results day inherited the results-day move, including transcripts,
  recording links and director changes filed the same evening. Now (a)
  routine, investor_meetings, earnings_call and unclassified rows never get a
  boost, and (b) a session's move goes only to that ticker's highest-scoring
  filing(s) reacting to it. Boosted rows: 50. MUST_READ: 70 → 51, of which
  27 are results (it's results season).
- **Scores are recomputed every run** (free), because the reaction session may
  not be in the price data yet when an announcement first arrives.

## D21 — 1-line "why it matters" summaries only where they pay off

- **Decision:** only MUST_READ and WORTH_A_LOOK rows get a summary, from
  `call_cheap`, batched 20 per call. ROUTINE rows get none.
- **Prompt rules:** use only facts in the text, never invent numbers, say what
  to check in the filing when the text is thin, no buy/sell advice, max 25
  words. The market reaction is included as context.
- **Known limitation:** NSE descriptions are often one line ("has submitted
  financial results"), so many summaries can only say *what to check*. Reading
  the PDF content would fix this; it's a candidate for a later step.
- **Cost so far:** 13 calls, 16,641 input + 8,796 output tokens, about $0.027
  (estimated at 2.5-flash rates; see D18).
EOF

open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)

Step 3 is committed (`a1855a0`); Step 4 isn't committed yet. I confirmed `.env` is git-ignored, and `backend/.env` doesn't show up in `git status`.

## Changes to your spec
- **Vertex AI is blocked.** Your key starts with `AQ.`, so it goes to Vertex as you specified, but Vertex returns 403 because its API isn't enabled on the key's Google Cloud project.
- **Gemini 2.5 models aren't available.** The same key works on the regular Gemini API, but `gemini-2.5-flash` and `gemini-2.5-pro` return 404 "no longer available to new users".
- **The model you picked was overloaded.** `gemini-3.8-flash` hit repeated "high demand" errors and took about 5 minutes per batch. I switched the cheap model to `gemini-3.5-flash`, which answered in 9–28s; the change is one line in `.env`. Two classification calls and three summary calls went through on 3.8-flash before the switch.
- **Strong model not chosen yet.** `gemini-4-argon` returned a quota error. Step 4 doesn't use the strong model, so I'll need your choice before a later step does.
- **ID-style change to the logging:** `call_cheap` and `call_strong` take an extra `feature=` argument, so cost can be broken down per feature in Step 12.
- **SDK retries off:** the SDK's own silent retries are turned off and each request has a 120s timeout, so my retry logic (which is logged) is the only retry layer.

## Rules vs LLM
| Method | Rows | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Rules (free) | **224 (80%)** | Examples: "Transcript" → earnings_call, "Schedule of meet" → investor_meetings, newspaper ads of results → routine |
| Cheap LLM | **57 (20%)** | 4 calls of up to 20 rows. These were genuinely vague: "General Updates", committee outcomes, rumour verifications, "Non Convertible Securities" allotments |

Nine rows stayed `unclassified` even after the LLM. They are vague "Disclosure under Regulation 30" filings.

## Ranking fix
The first version boosted 139 of 281 rows for market reaction. On a results day, every filing inherited the price move: transcripts, recording links, and director changes filed that evening. Now:
- **No boost for follow-ups:** routine, investor-meeting, earnings-call and unclassified rows never get a market boost.
- **One filing per move:** a price move is credited only to that stock's most important filing reacting to that session.
- **Bigger events score higher within a category:** equity raises (QIP, preferential, rights) and actual mergers get a bump. Plain NCD allotments and new subsidiaries drop to WORTH_A_LOOK.

Boosted rows fell from 139 to 50, and MUST_READ from 70 to 51 (27 of those are results). Final split: **MUST_READ 51 · WORTH_A_LOOK 86 · ROUTINE 144**.

## 10 examples
"Reaction" is the stock's move and volume (vs its 20-day average) on the first trading session after the filing.

| Tier | Score (boost) | Ticker | Category | By | Reaction | Filing | Why it matters (LLM) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MUST_READ | 100 (+25) | CAPLIPOINT | results | rules | −5.3% / 5.4x | Q2 financial results | Review the filed September 2026 quarterly results to assess recent revenue, profit margins, and operational performance. |
| MUST_READ | 85 (+10) | BAJFINANCE | fund_raise | rules | +3.4% / 1.2x | Outcome of QIP committee | Capital-raising developments are underway; check the filing for the issue price, funds raised, and equity dilution details. |
| MUST_READ | 80 (+20) | HDFCBANK | management_change | rules | +3.7% / 2.3x | Change in Management | Executive-level management changes can shift strategic execution; check the filing to identify the specific outgoing or incoming leadership personnel. |
| MUST_READ | 75 (+15) | SUNPHARMA | litigation | LLM | +0.2% / 2.8x | Exchange seeks clarification on news report | Regulatory scrutiny over alleged eye-care drug production halts directly affects plant operations and compliance; check the company's response. |
| WORTH_A_LOOK | 65 | TATASTEEL | M&A | rules | — | Acquisition of 38,222 shares via preference conversion | Conversion of 25,10,830 preference shares into 38,222 equity shares alters the company's direct equity ownership in Creative Port Development Private Limited. |
| WORTH_A_LOOK | 60 (+10) | NCC | capex | rules | +4.2% / 0.8x | Bagging/Receiving of orders | New order wins were reported, but shareholders must check the detailed filing to evaluate the contract values and execution timelines. |
| WORTH_A_LOOK | 55 (+10) | HINDUNILVR | dividend | rules | −0.1% / 2.1x | Interim dividend record date | Shares must be held prior to November 12, 2026, to qualify for the FY 2026-27 interim dividend. |
| ROUTINE | 30 | INFY | press_release | LLM | — | Infosys Prize winners announced | *(no summary)* |
| ROUTINE | 15 | RELIANCE | investor_meetings | rules | — | Execs at Morgan Stanley conference | *(no summary)* |

**Problem with the summaries:** many can only say *what to check* rather than what happened. That's because NSE's descriptions are often a single line like "has submitted financial results". Reading the PDFs would fix this, which I'd suggest for a later step.

"""Download exchange filing PDFs (cached) and extract their text with PyMuPDF."""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import logging
import random
import time
from pathlib import Path

import fitz  # PyMuPDF
import requests

from backend.data.announcements import USER_AGENT

BACKEND_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
PDF_CACHE_DIR = BACKEND_DIR / "cache" / "pdfs"
MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3
TIMEOUT = 60

log = logging.getLogger("finn.pdf")


class PDFError(RuntimeError):
    pass


def _headers(url: str) -> dict:
    referer = "https://www.bseindia.com/" if "bseindia" in url else "https://www.nseindia.com/"
    return {
        "User-Agent": USER_AGENT,
        "Accept": "application/pdf,application/octet-stream;q=0.9,*/*;q=0.8",
        "Accept-Language": "en-US,en;q=0.9",
        "Referer": referer,
    }


def cache_path(url: str) -> Path:
    return PDF_CACHE_DIR / f"{hashlib.sha1(url.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()}.pdf"


def download_pdf(url: str) -> Path:
    """Return a local path to the PDF, downloading it once (cached by URL)."""
    path = cache_path(url)
    if path.exists() and path.stat().st_size > 0:
        return path
    PDF_CACHE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    last_error: Exception | None = None
    for attempt in range(1, MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1):
        try:
            resp = requests.get(url, headers=_headers(url), timeout=TIMEOUT)
            if resp.status_code == 200 and resp.content[:5] == b"%PDF-":
                path.write_bytes(resp.content)
                time.sleep(random.uniform(0.5, 1.0))
                return path
            last_error = PDFError(f"HTTP {resp.status_code}, content-type {resp.headers.get('content-type')}")
        except requests.RequestException as exc:
            last_error = exc
        time.sleep(2 * attempt)
    raise PDFError(f"could not download {url}: {last_error}")


def page_texts(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Plain text of every page, in reading order."""
    with fitz.open(path) as doc:
        return [page.get_text("text", sort=True) for page in doc]


def is_scanned(texts: list[str]) -> bool:
    """True when the PDF has (almost) no text layer, i.e. it's scanned images."""
    return sum(len(t.strip()) for t in texts) < 200 * max(1, min(len(texts), 3))

"""Download exchange filing PDFs (cached) and extract their text with PyMuPDF."""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import logging
import random
import time
from pathlib import Path

import fitz  # PyMuPDF
import requests

from backend.data.announcements import USER_AGENT

BACKEND_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
PDF_CACHE_DIR = BACKEND_DIR / "cache" / "pdfs"
MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3
TIMEOUT = 60

log = logging.getLogger("finn.pdf")


class PDFError(RuntimeError):
    pass


def _headers(url: str) -> dict:
    referer = "https://www.bseindia.com/" if "bseindia" in url else "https://www.nseindia.com/"
    return {
        "User-Agent": USER_AGENT,
        "Accept": "application/pdf,application/octet-stream;q=0.9,*/*;q=0.8",
        "Accept-Language": "en-US,en;q=0.9",
        "Referer": referer,
    }


def cache_path(url: str) -> Path:
    return PDF_CACHE_DIR / f"{hashlib.sha1(url.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()}.pdf"


def download_pdf(url: str) -> Path:
    """Return a local path to the PDF, downloading it once (cached by URL)."""
    path = cache_path(url)
    if path.exists() and path.stat().st_size > 0:
        return path
    PDF_CACHE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    last_error: Exception | None = None
    for attempt in range(1, MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1):
        try:
            resp = requests.get(url, headers=_headers(url), timeout=TIMEOUT)
            if resp.status_code == 200 and resp.content[:5] == b"%PDF-":
                path.write_bytes(resp.content)
                time.sleep(random.uniform(0.5, 1.0))
                return path
            last_error = PDFError(f"HTTP {resp.status_code}, content-type {resp.headers.get('content-type')}")
        except requests.RequestException as exc:
            last_error = exc
        time.sleep(2 * attempt)
    raise PDFError(f"could not download {url}: {last_error}")


def page_texts(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Plain text of every page, in reading order."""
    with fitz.open(path) as doc:
        return [page.get_text("text", sort=True) for page in doc]


def is_scanned(texts: list[str]) -> bool:
    """True when the PDF has (almost) no text layer, i.e. it's scanned images."""
    return sum(len(t.strip()) for t in texts) < 200 * max(1, min(len(texts), 3))

# Usage logging
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _connect() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    DB_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    conn.execute(
        """
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS llm_usage (
            id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            feature       TEXT NOT NULL,
            model         TEXT NOT NULL,
            input_tokens  INTEGER NOT NULL,
            output_tokens INTEGER NOT NULL,   -- includes thinking tokens
            est_cost_usd  REAL NOT NULL,
            created_at    TEXT NOT NULL       -- UTC ISO timestamp
        )
        """
    )
    return conn


def estimate_cost(model: str, input_tokens: int, output_tokens: int) -> float:
    price_in, price_out = PRICING.get(model, DEFAULT_PRICE)
    return (input_tokens * price_in + output_tokens * price_out) / 1_000_000


def log_usage(feature: str, model: str, input_tokens: int, output_tokens: int) -> float:
    if model not in PRICING and model not in _unpriced_warned:
        _unpriced_warned.add(model)
        log.warning("No price listed for %s; estimating with gemini-2.5-flash rates.", model)
    cost = estimate_cost(model, input_tokens, output_tokens)
    with closing(_connect()) as conn:
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO llm_usage (feature, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, est_cost_usd, created_at) "
            "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (feature, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost,
             datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")),
        )
        conn.commit()
    return cost

def _generate(model: str, contents: str, config: types.GenerateContentConfig, feature: str,
              max_attempts: int = MAX_ATTEMPTS):
    """generate_content with retry/backoff; logs token usage. Returns the raw response."""
    delay = BASE_BACKOFF

            break

            if isinstance(exc, errors.APIError):
                code, retryable = exc.code, exc.code in RETRYABLE_CODES
            else:
                # Timeouts / dropped connections from the SDK's HTTP layer (no HTTP code).
                code, retryable = type(exc).__name__, _is_network_error(exc)
            if not retryable or attempt == max_attempts:
                error_cls = LLMQuotaError if code == 429 else LLMError
                raise error_cls(f"{model} failed ({code}): {getattr(exc, 'message', None) or exc}") from exc
            wait = delay + random.uniform(0, 1)
            log.warning("%s returned %s; retrying in %.1fs (attempt %d/%d)", model, code, wait, attempt, max_attempts)

"""Extract headline P&L numbers from quarterly results filings.

    python -m backend.pipeline.results_extract                   # all `results` filings with a PDF
    python -m backend.pipeline.results_extract --ticker INFY
    python -m backend.pipeline.results_extract --limit 5 --force

For each filing:
  1. Download the PDF (cached in backend/cache/pdfs/; BSE copy if the NSE one is broken).
  2. Pick the pages holding the P&L table (consolidated preferred), max 8 pages.
  3. cheap LLM -> strict JSON of raw line items for current / previous / year-ago quarter.
  4. Python: verify every number actually appears in the PDF text (anything that
     doesn't is nulled), derive EBITDA if not stated, compute QoQ / YoY / margins.
Results are cached in `results_enrichment`, keyed by pdf_url.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import re
import sqlite3
from contextlib import closing
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from backend import llm
from backend.data.prices import DB_PATH
from backend.pipeline.pdf_utils import PDFError, is_scanned, load_filing

log = logging.getLogger("finn.results")

MAX_PAGES = 8
PAGE_CHAR_LIMIT = 9000
PERIODS = ("current_qtr", "prev_qtr", "yoy_qtr")
LINE_ITEMS = ("revenue", "ebitda_reported", "finance_costs", "depreciation", "pbt", "pat")
METRICS = ("revenue", "ebitda", "pbt", "pat")

PNL_PAGE = re.compile(r"profit\s*/?\s*\(?loss\)?\s*before\s*(exceptional\s*items\s*and\s*)?tax|profit before tax", re.I)
INCOME_LINE = re.compile(r"revenue from operations|total income|interest earned|income from operations", re.I)
CONSOLIDATED = re.compile(r"consolidated", re.I)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Page selection
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def select_pages(texts: list[str]) -> tuple[list[int], str]:
    """Indices of pages to send and the basis they were chosen for.

    Results tables are often far from the start (ICICI p.13, INFY p.18 of 195),
    so instead of "first N pages" we take the first P&L statement page (and the
    one after it, where statements spill over), preferring a consolidated one.
    Falls back to the first pages for press releases without a SEBI-format table.
    """
    pnl = [i for i, t in enumerate(texts) if PNL_PAGE.search(t) and INCOME_LINE.search(t)]
    consolidated = [i for i in pnl if CONSOLIDATED.search(texts[i][:1500])]
    if consolidated or pnl:
        start = (consolidated or pnl)[0]
        pages = [start] + [i for i in (start + 1,) if i < len(texts)]
        # Add the standalone/consolidated counterpart's first page only if no consolidated table exists.
        return pages[:MAX_PAGES], "consolidated" if consolidated else "standalone_or_unknown"
    return list(range(min(len(texts), 6))), "no_pnl_table_found"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# LLM extraction
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
_NUM = {"type": ["number", "null"]}
_PERIOD = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {item: _NUM for item in LINE_ITEMS} | {"period_end": {"type": ["string", "null"]}},
    "required": [*LINE_ITEMS, "period_end"],
}
EXTRACT_SCHEMA = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "has_numbers": {"type": "boolean"},
        "is_financial_institution": {"type": "boolean"},
        "basis": {"type": ["string", "null"], "enum": ["consolidated", "standalone", None]},
        "currency_unit": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
        "period_label": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
        "current_qtr": _PERIOD,
        "prev_qtr": _PERIOD,
        "yoy_qtr": _PERIOD,
        "notes": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
    },
    "required": ["has_numbers", "is_financial_institution", "basis", "currency_unit", "period_label",
                 *PERIODS, "notes"],
}

PROMPT = """You extract numbers from an Indian listed company's quarterly results filing (text below, extracted from PDF).

Return JSON only. STRICT RULES:
- Use ONLY numbers written in the text. Copy them exactly as printed (drop thousands separators).
  Never calculate, estimate, convert units, or fill gaps. If a value is not printed, return null.
- Negative numbers are often printed in brackets, e.g. (12.5) -> -12.5.
- Columns in these tables are usually: current quarter, preceding quarter, same quarter of the
  previous year, then half-year / nine-month / full-year columns. Use ONLY the three quarter columns:
  current_qtr, prev_qtr (preceding quarter) and yoy_qtr (same quarter last year).
- If both consolidated and standalone statements are present, use consolidated. Set `basis`.
- Line items:
  revenue: "Revenue from operations". For banks/NBFCs/insurers (is_financial_institution=true) use
           "Total income" (or "Total revenue"); if only its parts are printed, return null.
  ebitda_reported: only if a line explicitly labelled EBITDA is printed in the table; else null.
  finance_costs: "Finance costs" (for banks: null; interest expended is not a finance cost here).
  depreciation: "Depreciation and amortisation expense".
  pbt: "Profit before tax" (after exceptional items, before tax).
  pat: "Net profit for the period" / "Profit after tax" for the whole entity (before other
       comprehensive income; for consolidated, the total before attributing to minority interest).
- period_end per column as YYYY-MM-DD if the column date is printed.
- currency_unit as printed, e.g. "INR Crores", "INR Lakhs", "INR Millions".
- period_label like "Q2 FY27" (Indian fiscal year: Apr-Mar; quarter ending 30 Sep 2026 = Q2 FY27).
- If the text has no quarterly financial table (e.g. a board-meeting notice, newspaper ad, or a press
  release without a table), set has_numbers=false, leave numbers null, and explain briefly in notes.
- notes: one short line on anything a reader should know (e.g. exceptional items, restated figures).

Company: {ticker}
Filing text:
{text}
"""


def extract_with_llm(ticker: str, text: str) -> dict:
    return llm.call_cheap(PROMPT.format(ticker=ticker, text=text), EXTRACT_SCHEMA, feature="results_extract")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Verification + derived metrics (pure Python)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def numbers_in_text(text: str) -> set[float]:
    """Every number printed in the text, tolerant of PDF artefacts like '21 .62' / '48 ,03'."""
    t = re.sub(r"(?<=\d)\s+(?=[.,]\s*\d)", "", text)          # '21 .62' -> '21.62'
    t = re.sub(r"(?<=\d[.,])\s+(?=\d)", "", t)                 # '48, 03' -> '48,03'
    values = set()
    for m in re.finditer(r"\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?", t):
        token = m.group(0)
        # A comma followed by exactly two digits at the end is an OCR'd decimal ('48,03' -> 48.03).
        if re.fullmatch(r"\d+,\d{2}", token):
            values.add(float(token.replace(",", ".")))
        try:
            values.add(float(token.replace(",", "")))
        except ValueError:
            pass
    return values


def verify(extracted: dict, text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Null out any number that isn't printed in the source text. Returns the removed fields."""
    printed = numbers_in_text(text)
    removed = []
    for period in PERIODS:
        for item in LINE_ITEMS:
            value = extracted.get(period, {}).get(item)
            if value is None:
                continue

    python -m backend.pipeline.results_extract                   # all `results` filings with a PDF

  2. Pick the pages holding the P&L table (consolidated preferred), max 8 pages.
  3. cheap LLM -> strict JSON of raw line items for current / previous / year-ago quarter.
  4. Python: verify every number actually appears in the PDF text (anything that
     doesn't is nulled), derive EBITDA if not stated, compute QoQ / YoY / margins.

MAX_PAGES = 8
PAGE_CHAR_LIMIT = 9000
PERIODS = ("current_qtr", "prev_qtr", "yoy_qtr")
LINE_ITEMS = ("revenue", "ebitda_reported", "finance_costs", "depreciation", "pbt", "pat")
METRICS = ("revenue", "ebitda", "pbt", "pat")

PNL_PAGE = re.compile(r"profit\s*/?\s*\(?loss\)?\s*before\s*(exceptional\s*items\s*and\s*)?tax|profit before tax", re.I)
INCOME_LINE = re.compile(r"revenue from operations|total income|interest earned|income from operations", re.I)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Page selection
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def select_pages(texts: list[str]) -> tuple[list[int], str]:
    """Indices of pages to send and the basis they were chosen for.

    Results tables are often far from the start (ICICI p.13, INFY p.18 of 195),
    so instead of "first N pages" we take the first P&L statement page (and the
    one after it, where statements spill over), preferring a consolidated one.
    Falls back to the first pages for press releases without a SEBI-format table.
    """
    pnl = [i for i, t in enumerate(texts) if PNL_PAGE.search(t) and INCOME_LINE.search(t)]
    consolidated = [i for i in pnl if CONSOLIDATED.search(texts[i][:1500])]
    if consolidated or pnl:
        start = (consolidated or pnl)[0]
        pages = [start] + [i for i in (start + 1,) if i < len(texts)]
        # Add the standalone/consolidated counterpart's first page only if no consolidated table exists.
        return pages[:MAX_PAGES], "consolidated" if consolidated else "standalone_or_unknown"
    return list(range(min(len(texts), 6))), "no_pnl_table_found"

    "type": "object",
    "properties": {item: _NUM for item in LINE_ITEMS} | {"period_end": {"type": ["string", "null"]}},
    "required": [*LINE_ITEMS, "period_end"],
}

    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "has_numbers": {"type": "boolean"},
        "is_financial_institution": {"type": "boolean"},
        "basis": {"type": ["string", "null"], "enum": ["consolidated", "standalone", None]},
        "currency_unit": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
        "period_label": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
        "current_qtr": _PERIOD,
        "prev_qtr": _PERIOD,
        "yoy_qtr": _PERIOD,
        "notes": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
    },
    "required": ["has_numbers", "is_financial_institution", "basis", "currency_unit", "period_label",

PROMPT = """You extract numbers from an Indian listed company's quarterly results filing (text below, extracted from PDF).

Return JSON only. STRICT RULES:
- Use ONLY numbers written in the text. Copy them exactly as printed (drop thousands separators).
  Never calculate, estimate, convert units, or fill gaps. If a value is not printed, return null.
- Negative numbers are often printed in brackets, e.g. (12.5) -> -12.5.
- Columns in these tables are usually: current quarter, preceding quarter, same quarter of the
  previous year, then half-year / nine-month / full-year columns. Use ONLY the three quarter columns:
  current_qtr, prev_qtr (preceding quarter) and yoy_qtr (same quarter last year).
- If both consolidated and standalone statements are present, use consolidated. Set `basis`.
- Line items:
  revenue: "Revenue from operations". For banks/NBFCs/insurers (is_financial_institution=true) use
           "Total income" (or "Total revenue"); if only its parts are printed, return null.
  ebitda_reported: only if a line explicitly labelled EBITDA is printed in the table; else null.
  finance_costs: "Finance costs" (for banks: null; interest expended is not a finance cost here).
  depreciation: "Depreciation and amortisation expense".
  pbt: "Profit before tax" (after exceptional items, before tax).

       comprehensive income; for consolidated, the total before attributing to minority interest).

- currency_unit as printed, e.g. "INR Crores", "INR Lakhs", "INR Millions".
- period_label like "Q2 FY27" (Indian fiscal year: Apr-Mar; quarter ending 30 Sep 2026 = Q2 FY27).

  release without a table), set has_numbers=false, leave numbers null, and explain briefly in notes.
- notes: one short line on anything a reader should know (e.g. exceptional items, restated figures).

Filing text:
{text}

def numbers_in_text(text: str) -> set[float]:

    t = re.sub(r"(?<=\d)\s+(?=[.,]\s*\d)", "", text)          # '21 .62' -> '21.62'
    t = re.sub(r"(?<=\d[.,])\s+(?=\d)", "", t)                 # '48, 03' -> '48,03'

    for m in re.finditer(r"\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?", t):
        token = m.group(0)
        # A comma followed by exactly two digits at the end is an OCR'd decimal ('48,03' -> 48.03).
        if re.fullmatch(r"\d+,\d{2}", token):
            values.add(float(token.replace(",", ".")))
        try:
            values.add(float(token.replace(",", "")))
        except ValueError:

    return values
